title: ChipletEM: Physics-Based 2.5D and 3D Chiplet Heterogeneous Integration Electromigration Signoff Tool Using Coupled Stress and Thermal Simulation
problem: Electromigration (EM) in 2.5D/3D chiplet heterogeneous integration systems is inadequately understood; existing EM research ignores Through Silicon Vias (TSVs) and non-uniform thermal distribution between dies, causing signoff errors and missing critical failure modes.
motivation: Advanced chiplet integration introduces new EM failure mechanisms not present in 2D designs; accurate EM modeling is essential for reliability signoff in high-density 2.5D/3D systems.
method: The tool simulates metal erosion in stacked chips (2.5D/3D chiplet systems) by running electrical and thermal models together, updating them at each time step. It uses FVM (finite volume method—splitting space into small regions to calculate heat distribution) to map temperature and current in the vertical connections between dies (TSVs), and FDTD (finite difference time domain—a grid-based solver) to track stress buildup and void nucleation and growth. As simulation progresses, these effects reinforce each other: current causes heat (Joule heating), which accelerates metal migration and void growth; voids increase electrical resistance, which changes voltage drop (IR drop) and generates more heat, which shifts mechanical stress—making it possible to catch failure modes that treating each effect separately would miss.
key_novelty: This tool is the first to simulate metal erosion in the vertical connections (TSVs) between stacked chips (2.5D/3D chiplets) by jointly modeling electrical flow, heat, stress, and void growth—effects that previous tools treated separately or ignored.
contributions: FVM-FDTD coupled electrical-thermal-stress simulation for 2.5D/3D chiplet EM
Analytical TSV thermal solver for accurate temperature distribution modeling
Multi-physics coupling of EM, thermal, and stress effects at each timestep
0.61% nucleation phase error, 2.4% growth phase error vs. FEM, 5.24% improvement vs. AFD method (from 22.22%)

metrics.accuracy: 0.61% nucleation error, 2.4% growth error vs. FEM, 17% improvement vs. AFD

primary_theme: Physics-based EM signoff tool for 2.5D/3D chiplet systems
